title: WoW: Forever Wraps the Biggest Beta in Franchise History
summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever just concluded "the largest beta in franchise history," according to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. That is a notable milestone for the long-running online game.

Blizzard recently bundled beta access with both the War Within and Midnight expansions, opening it up to players who want to pay for it. Previously, getting in was purely an opt-in-and-hope-Blizzard-picks-you process. Unofficial tool ClassicPlus.io suggests that over one million characters were created during the beta.

Developer Josh Greenfield called the turnout "the craziest numbers I've seen in 17 years working at Blizzard and almost 8 years on classic." In a post on September 18, 2026, he wrote: "Man, it was hard to sleep last night, I was so excited. Beta has been... crazy... We've got something really special here."

World of Warcraft: Forever was announced at BlizzCon earlier this year after months of rumors, as a sort of "alternate universe" World of Warcraft: set in the world of the original game, but taking different twists and turns with its plot, mechanics, and content. The beta ran from September 17 through October 23, and the full game launches on November 4, available to anyone with an existing World of Warcraft subscription. The release has been highly anticipated, following high praise for the original World of Warcraft Classic launch several years ago and the popular Season of Discovery game mode, which served as a sort of proto-WoW: Forever for a limited time.
why_it_matters: The huge beta shows how much demand there is for a fresh take on a long-running game, and its success could shape how Blizzard revives older games for loyal players.

background_read: World of Warcraft is a long-running online game in which players create characters and explore a shared fantasy world together.
A beta is a test version of a game that players try before the full release, so makers can find problems and learn what players enjoy.
An expansion adds new stories, places and challenges to a game that players already know, and a subscription lets players keep playing for as long as they pay to stay in the game.
